name: collapse-slides-rather-than-reflows
description:
Hiding the sidebar animated the SLOT's width, and the page inside was laid out at 100% - so every tick re-laid-out the whole document. The favourites grid re-flowed its auto-fill columns and the rows re-wrapped, which is what the reporter saw as the icons changing position rather than the sidebar sliding away.

The lab never animates width. Its hidden sidebar is held at a fixed width and moved with transform (swipe-lab.html:37-39), so nothing inside it can move relative to anything else.

The page is now held at the docked width the native side pushes, and hangs off the trailing edge, so a narrowing slot slides it out and clips it. This captures the middle of the collapse, which is the only moment the difference exists: at either end the sidebar is simply present or absent.

actions.note: first paint, and the sidebar announces itself
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
the sidebar at rest, so the mid-collapse frame has something to be compared against by eye
THE capture. The collapse animation runs about 150ms, so a capture started with the chord catches it in flight. 30fps to get several frames inside that window.

assertions.label: the-window-survived-the-collapse
assertions.desc: Liveness. The frames are the point of this scenario and a person reads them, but a run that crashed would otherwise leave three captures nobody questions.

assertions.label: the-collapse-actually-ran
assertions.desc: The floor. The grip band is re-placed on every layout pass, so its presence says the sidebar laid out at all - without it a chord that missed would leave a still frame that looks like a perfect slide.
